newsitem.title: UK: Safeway extends losses on trading statement.
newsitem.headline: Safeway extends losses on trading statement.

text.p: Shares in Safeway Plc extended their pre-market losses at the start of trading on Friday as the market took fright at a cautious trading statement from the supermarket operator and marked shares lower across the sector.

"What has spooked the sector is the comment that things have slowed since the start of the New Year," said one senior trader. "We have shaved our profit forecast for Safeway by 10 million pounds to 430 million stg."

He said there were continuing concerns that the supermarket sector could see intensified price competition but pointed out that supermarket shares were a little vulnerable to profit-taking having recently had a good run.
"I don't think this statement should worry people too much," the dealer said, "we would be looking to pick up Safeway on any further weakness, but for the moment it has certainly spooked the sector."
Safeway shares were down 18p at 371 by 0843 GMT. Other supermarket stocks also fell, with Tesco Plc down 11p at 352, J Sainsbury Plc off 3p at 325-1/2 and ASDA Group Plc 3-1/2p lower at 117-1/2.

In a statement, Safeway warned that profits could be hit by a slowdown in sales growth in the first 16 weeks of the second half of the current year. Over the first 16 weeks of the second half, which ends in March, and "in common with the sector, sales growth in existing stores has slowed", the company said.

"Were this to continue, profits for the remaining eight weeks of the current year might be affected," it added. "Nevertheless we are confident that Safeway is well positioned to deliver a further year of solid profit growth."
In the year to March 1996 Safeway posted pre-tax profits of 429.4 million stg.
Safeway shares reached a peak of 430p on January 14, their highest in over four years.
